topic: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas

outline.topic: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: The Bridge Between Slopes and Areas

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
sections.content: Briefly revisit differentiation as finding the slope (velocity) and integration as finding the area (total distance). Use a graphical animation showing a car's speedometer vs. odometer.
sections.example: A delivery drone's velocity curve vs. its cumulative distance traveled.

sections.title: The Conceptual Link: Accumulation Functions
sections.content: Introduce the area function A(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt. Visualize this as a 'sliding curtain' moving across a graph, covering area as 'x' increases.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering nuts: The rate of gathering (nuts/minute) integrated over time gives the total nut pile size.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1): The Inverse Relationship
sections.content: Explain that the derivative of the accumulation function is the original function: d/dx [∫[a to x] f(t) dt] = f(x). Graphically demonstrate that the tiny change in area is just a narrow rectangular strip of height f(x).
sections.example: If the rate of water flow into a tank is f(t), the rate of change of the tank's volume is exactly the current flow rate.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2): Evaluating Definite Integrals
sections.content: Define the relationship: ∫[a to b] f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is the antiderivative. This connects the 'net change' to the 'anti-slope'.
sections.example: A rocket's position at time 'b' minus its position at time 'a' equals the integral of its velocity function between those times.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that differentiation and integration are reverse processes (inverse operations). Display a circular animation showing the transition from f(x) to F(x) and back.
sections.example: A game character: Differentiation takes you from position to velocity; Integration takes you from velocity back to position.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: The Two Pillars
lecture_lines: Differentiation measures the slope of a curve.
Integration calculates the total area under a curve.
Velocity is the derivative of position.
animations: Fade in text: The Two Pillars (Calculus). Color #FFFFFF.
Draw connection line between Derivative and Integral. Color #FF00FF.
Highlight 'Derivative' pillar with a soft yellow glow. Color #FFFF00.
Highlight 'Integral' pillar with a soft blue glow. Color #00FFFF.
Label both pillars clearly: 'Rate' and 'Accumulation'. Color #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Conceptual Link: Accumulation Functions
lecture_lines: A(x) represents the area under f(t).
A(x) is the integral from a to x.
animations: Display accumulation function F(x) = ∫ f(t)dt. Color #FFFFFF.
Animate area under curve f(t) growing as x moves right. Color #00FF00.
Label the instantaneous height of area as f(x). Color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 1): The Inverse Relationship
lecture_lines: The derivative of area is the height.
This reveals the inverse relationship of calculus.
The area changes at rate f(x).
Calculus connects local slopes to total area.
animations: Animate small delta change in x and corresponding area delta. Color #FFFF00.
Show derivative of accumulation area equals original curve height. Color #FF0000.

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem (Part 2): Evaluating Definite Integrals
lecture_lines: Definite integrals measure total net change.
F(b) minus F(a) yields the integral.
The antiderivative evaluates definite integrals directly.
It bridges derivatives with integral values.
animations: Show formula: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = F(b) - F(a). Color #FFFFFF.
Highlight F(b) and F(a) on a graph. Color #00FFFF.
Highlight total accumulated area between a and b. Color #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Calculus links slopes and areas together.
Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
animations: Display list: Derivative and Integral are inverse processes. Color #FFFFFF.
Summarize: Accumulation functions link these two major pillars. Color #FFFF00.
Show concluding 'Fundamental Theorem' text center screen. Color #00FF00.
